SearchAliases: Yunmen cut off all streams phrase
Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support the stream-cutting image; it is a phrase-function and evaluative capacity, not a literal hydrological claim or guaranteed final station.

Senses.Explanation: Records use this phrase for words or actions that stop proliferating routes of discrimination and response. The image is “cut off all streams,” and Yunmen-house discussions place it among three phrase-functions alongside covering heaven and earth and following wave after wave. Yuanwu Keqin calls it a solitary voicing of the hidden pivot that cuts off all streams without constraint or turning back. In the Blue Cliff Record he explains that an ordinary Yunmen phrase must contain three phrases: one that covers heaven and earth, one that follows the waves, and one that cuts off all streams. Ruibai Mingxue says that in a single shout the cutting-off phrase sweeps away ordinary and sage and ends conceptual interpretation. Hanyue Fazang describes unconstrained movement as lion-like and stream-cutting, while Feiyin Tongrong pairs the image with a sword across the sky and an iron pillar. Shiyu Mingfang applies it to the power of a fragrant elephant crossing beyond the mind-ocean. Tianyin Yuanxiu nevertheless says that even cutting off all streams remains outside the gate, preventing the phrase from becoming a final attainment-label.

Not yet; not there yet: in the Chan corpus this is especially frequent as a teaching-seat verdict on a reply, shout, verse, or claimed understanding. The exact words (未在) also retain their ordinary temporal force. Zhaozhou Congshen says, 'Not there yet; say more' (未在更道). Gufeng Xiu tells Wanshan Zhengning, 'You have got it, but you are still not there yet' (你也得，只是未在). Fushi Tongxian likewise says, 'Not there yet; say more,' while Tianyin Yuanxiu uses the phrase to reject an attempted deception. Guangxiao Huijue says, 'Even if you reached a thousand years, you still would not yet be old' (直至千歲也未在). Thus the corpus deploys one phrase both as an evaluative reply and in ordinary statements of something not yet reached or completed.
Senses.Note: The exact headword occurs 1,247 times in 255 allowlisted texts. Searches found no self-defining formula equivalent to 'the so-called not-there-yet,' 'it is called not-there-yet,' or 'what is meant by not-there-yet?' The repeated collocation 'not there yet; say more' (未在更道) occurs 72 times in 39 texts, while 'you have got it, but are still not there yet' (你也得，只是未在) displays a further recorded shape. The subject left incomplete is sometimes named, as in 'the matter beyond is not there yet' (向上事未在).
